reasoning_summary:
55: Merrill prints lines 23-32 (the piece often numbered 58b) right after line 13, then 14-22; the records' order is kept and noted. The cruces in 9 ('A velte') and 11 ('reduc') are kept untranslated with notes; Merrill's 'vi vis' in 21 is rendered as 'if you wish' (si vis), with a note.
51: the lost line 8 keeps '. . . .' with a note; quod in line 5 is neuter (the whole scene) and misero is split from mihi as the lines stand; lumina is kept as 'the lights' (eyes).
54: fragmentary; the '*' gap lines are kept, 'eri' is noted as corrupt or a name, peditum is 'fart', recoctus 're-cooked' (rejuvenated).
56-59: obscenity rendered plainly: trusantem 'thrusting', rigida mea ... cecidi 'with my stiff one I struck' (noted as fucking him), cinaedi 'catamites', pathico 'the buggered one' (noted as ambiguous between Mamurra and Caesar), glubit 'peels' (noted: skins back foreskins), fellat 'sucks off'; salaputium (53) as 'little prick', noted as uncertain.
52.3: perierat read as peierat 'swears falsely', with the alternative 'had perished' noted. 45.17: source misprint 'Arnor' kept in the Latin and rendered 'Love'.
Metaphors kept literal with notes: sinistrae 'left hands' (thieves, 47), ocelle 'little eye' (darling, 50), corona 'ring' (53), tenebrae 'darknesses' (55). Run-over clauses (45.3-4, 50.14-16, 51.3-6, 55.29-32) are split by what stands on each line.
